title_en: Building a Berkshire for the Middle Market – Tracy Britt Cool (EP.521)
title_zh: 为中型市场打造 Berkshire —— Tracy Britt Cool 与她的长期合伙平台 Canvas（EP.521）
subtitle_zh: Berkshire 前高管 Tracy Britt Cool 创办 Canvas：用 15 年以上长期结构、业务系统与 4,000 人 CEO 社群，做家族中型企业的伯克希尔式归宿。
summary_zh: 本期 Capital Allocators 由 Ted Seides 对话 Tracy Britt Cool——长期投资合伙机构 Canvas 的联合创始人（转写误作 Canbrick），为家族持有的中型企业所有者提供传统私募股权之外的差异化归宿。Tracy 曾在 Berkshire Hathaway 工作十年，是 Warren Buffett 为数不多的副手之一：商学院毕业即任其财务助理，出任多家被投公司董事长，并担任 Pampered Chef 的 CEO。节目核心是把 Berkshire 式的长期主义与运营经验移植到中型市场：她复盘 Pampered Chef 的大翻身——原以为一两年能扭转下滑十年的业务，实际花了近四年，深刻体会到做运营一切都比表格里更难，因为全都关系到人。Canvas 的差异化在于超长持有期、以双边协商而非拍卖流程定制双赢结构，以及一个拥有约 4,000 名高管的社群，在招聘、运营与增长上分享最佳实践；目标锁定 EBITDA 在 500 万至 5,000 万美元、有护城河（moat）与可量化竞争优势的家族企业。她引用 Buffett 所说约 50% 的招聘是错误的，强调把业务系统与 KPI 植入企业、帮其在组织内部长出肌肉，正因持有期长才值得。她认为 AI 时代人、文化与关系反而更重要。

I grew up on a family farm. My dad did nothing in investing except for he invested in soybean futures to hedge his position on the farm. That was my first exposure. I didn't fully understand commodity investing is a bit different than what I got interested in. Then over time,
turns.zh: Tracy，见到你真高兴。很荣幸来到这里，非常感谢你的邀请。我想请你带我回到最初——你对投资和企业生意的兴趣是从哪里来的？我是在家庭农场长大的。我父亲和投资唯一的交集，就是在农场上用大豆期货对冲头寸，那是我的第一次接触。我当时并没有完全理解——商品投资和后来让我着迷的东西不太一样。再后来，

turns.en: when I went to college, I found Warren Buffett. I started reading a lot. I naturally gravitated towards it, building great businesses, finding companies that are undervalued, investing in them.
turns.zh: 我上了大学，遇到了 Warren Buffett。我开始大量阅读，自然而然地被吸引——打造伟大的企业，发现被低估的公司，然后投资它们。

turns.en: That concept resonated with me early on. It was rare that somebody picks up that material, then they find a way to connect with Warren. Walk me through that story, how that all happened.
turns.zh: 这个理念很早就与我共鸣。很少有人会对这类材料产生兴趣，然后还能找到办法与 Warren 建立联系。给我讲讲那个故事是怎么发生的。

turns.en: I started out writing to investors that I admired and respected, that I wanted to learn from, CEOs of different firms on Wall Street. I wrote a letter to Warren asking to bring a group of students out to Omaha. I had started a nonprofit focused on investment education for women.
turns.zh: 我一开始是给那些我敬佩、尊重、想向他们学习的投资人写信——华尔街不同公司的 CEO。我给 Warren 写了一封信，想带一群学生去奥马哈。我当时创办了一个专注女性投资教育的非营利组织。

turns.en: He had had MBA students come, but he hadn't had undergrads. He generously said yes, and we brought a group of students out to Omaha. What happened from there? I got to know him a little bit through it, planned that trip three or four times. When I graduated business school, wrote him another letter, asked if I could come out a day a week a month and pick his brain, assuming he'd say no. Unfortunately, he said yes. I spent my post MBA summer working with him. In the summer,
turns.zh: 他接待过 MBA 学生，但没接待过本科生。他非常慷慨地答应了，我们带一群学生去了奥马哈。从那之后发生了什么？通过这件事我对他有了些了解，那次行程我前后操办了三四次。商学院毕业时，我又给他写了一封信，问能不能每月去一天向他请教，我以为他会拒绝。结果他说好。MBA 毕业后的那个夏天，我就在他身边工作。夏天结束时，

turns.en: he said, I'd love to hire you. I just don't have a role. Berkshire's 25 people at headquarters. I started my full-time job, and he called a few weeks later and said, if you're interested, I'll create a role for you to join. Quit my job and moved out to Omaha later that year.
turns.zh: 他说：我很想雇用你，只是没有现成的岗位——Berkshire 总部只有 25 个人。我开始做另一份全职工作，几周后他打来电话说，如果你愿意，我可以为你创建一个岗位。我辞了工作，那年晚些时候搬到了奥马哈。

turns.en: What do you think it was, or maybe what did he tell you after the fact, it's so rare that that would have happened, if at all? Warren's always been very open at bringing people into his life at different stages. He was nearly 80 when I joined Berkshire. To trust me at that age was something special. I never asked him specifically why. Probably a combination of grit, resiliency, willingness to work hard,
turns.zh: 你觉得是什么促成了这一切——或者事后他告诉过你吗？这种事太罕见了。Warren 一向乐于在不同人生阶段把人带进他的生活。我加入 Berkshire 时他已经快 80 岁了。在那个年纪还信任我，是很特别的事。我从来没具体问过他为什么。大概是毅力、韧性、愿意拼命干活，

turns.en: personality, those dynamics that came together. I had a number of people over the years write me letters. Occasionally, they stood out to me too. My partner, Brian Humphrey, wrote me a letter when he was in Stanford at business school. That's how I met him. For some reason, that letter resonated with me in what he was sharing and was doing. It's hard to put your finger on it, but you know it when you see it. If you're giving advice to people who are asking you about how to approach
turns.zh: 加上性格，这些因素凑在了一起。这些年也有人给我写信，偶尔也有人让我眼前一亮。我的合伙人 Brian Humphrey 在斯坦福读商学院时给我写过一封信，我就是那样认识他的。不知为什么，那封信里他分享的东西、正在做的事，与我产生了共鸣。这种东西很难说清楚，但你看到就知道。如果有人来问你，该如何去接近

turns.en: someone that they admire, is there anything that you've been able to pull from the ones that resonated for you? One is you want to try to find a mutual connection. You're from the same town. turns.zh: 你敬佩的人，你能从那些曾经打动你的经历里总结出什么吗？第一，尽量找到共同联系——你们来自同一个小镇，兴趣相似，同一个学校、同样的爱好；保持谦逊，做你自己；绝对不要用 AI 生成，不要给 30 个人发同一封信，要定制；纸质信比发邮件或在

turns.en: LinkedIn because that's so pervasive these days, it doesn't stand out. When you showed up at Omaha, what was the job as the 26th employee? I was Warren's chief of staff. I spent time working on anything that crosses desks looking at investments. I worked on insurance deals, acquisitions, a variety of things. It was just an opportunity for me to learn and grow, which was remarkable.
turns.zh: LinkedIn 上发私信有效得多，因为现在 LinkedIn 太普遍了，根本不起眼。你到奥马哈的时候，作为第 26 名员工，工作是干什么？我担任 Warren 的幕僚长 (chief of staff)，处理各种跨到他桌面的事情，研究投资，做过保险交易、收购，各种各样的事。那是一个让我学习和成长的机会，非常了不起。

turns.en: What did that feel like day to day? There was a lot of responsibility. I joked. Warren had a few IQ points on me as well as 50 years of experience, so I had a lot to catch up on. I spent a lot of time reading, learning, working late, trying to understand our businesses at Berkshire, why we invested, and then what worked, what didn't work. Warren was very gracious to spending time with me, going to lunch, talking about those companies in detail. That helped me become a better investor,
turns.zh: 日常是什么感觉？责任很重。我常开玩笑说，Warren 比我多几个 IQ 点，还多 50 年的经验，所以我有太多要追赶的。我花大量时间阅读、学习、加班，试图理解 Berkshire 的各个业务，我们为什么投资，什么有效、什么无效。Warren 非常慷慨地花时间陪我，一起吃午饭，详细聊那些公司。这让我成为一个更好的投资人，

turns.en: more thoughtful in what I was doing. The day to day work was what was coming across his desk. It varied widely. It was going deep on a variety of topics that there was some need or some interest on the Berkshire side.
turns.zh: 让我做的每件事都更有章法。日常工作就是来到他桌上的事情，跨度非常大——在 Berkshire 有需要或有兴趣的各种话题上深挖。

turns.en: How did your time there transition from pure investing to jumping into some of the portfolio companies? When I was at Berkshire, I would travel and meet some of the companies. Warren started asking me my thoughts on the businesses. The first was Larson Jewel, which is a custom framing business. Then there was Benjamin Moore, Oriental Trading Company, Johns Manville, and others. As I did that, Warren asked me to come in and a chairman role. Typically,
turns.zh: 你在那里是怎么从纯投资过渡到介入一些被投公司的？在 Berkshire 的时候，我会出差去拜访一些公司。Warren 开始问我对这些业务的看法。第一家是 Rand's Jewelers，一家相框定制生意。然后是 Benjamin Moore、Oriental Trading Company、Johns Manville 等等。做着做着，Warren 让我进去担任董事长。通常来说，

turns.zh: 那些业务往往是公司没有发挥全部潜力的，有机会去帮忙。我会站到管理团队身边，帮他们看清楚并走出困境；有些情况下，也会更换管理团队来配合。

turns.en: That was my first foray into operating. As I did that, what I realized was that there was going to be more value created on the operating side going forward. In the buyout world, the days of buying businesses for seven times and selling them for 12 a few years later was probably gone, and you needed to add more value. I thought to myself, if I go get operating experience, I'll be a much better investor. I'll have more credibility, more empathy, more ability to help
turns.zh: 那是我第一次踏入运营。做着做着，我意识到未来更多的价值会在运营端创造。在收购 (buyout) 世界里，用 7 倍 EBITDA 买入、几年后 12 倍卖出的日子大概已经过去，你必须创造更多价值。我心想，如果我去积累运营经验，我会成为一个更好的投资人——会有更多可信度、更多同理心、更有能力去帮助

turns.en: these businesses. That was the turning point in my mind of this power and this shift that was happening in investing and operating. I'd love you to walk me through a story or two in your time at Berkshire of those operating roles. Benjamin Moore, I was chair of that business. Benjamin Moore is an amazing brand built over 100 plus years, tangible, sold through a dealer network.
turns.zh: 这些企业。那是我思想里的一个转折点——投资和运营之间的权力和重心正在转移。你能给我讲一两个你在 Berkshire 担任运营角色的故事吗？Benjamin Moore——我担任过那家公司的主席。Benjamin Moore 是一个一百多年打造出来的了不起的品牌，实实在在，通过经销商网络销售。

turns.en: Over a 10-year period, it had lost its way. Volume growth in terms of gallons had come down considerably. Earnings were relatively flat. The business was cutting marketing spend, taking price to maintain earnings instead of investing in the channel, investing in marketing, investing in the brand, which is critical in that type of business. When I joined, it was this opportunity. How do we reinvest in the core part of the business? If we do that well,
turns.zh: 在 10 年的时间里，它迷失了方向。以加仑计的销量大幅下滑，盈利大体持平。公司在削减营销开支、靠提价来维持利润，而不是投资渠道、投资营销、投资品牌——在那类业务里品牌恰恰是关键。我加入的时候，机会就在于：我们如何重新投资业务的核心？如果我们做好了，

turns.en: we can reposition the stores as leaders in their space. We can reinvest in our dealers and see the specialness of that over the time we significantly improved the earnings of the business while strengthening the channel, driving it through volume growth, not just financial engineering.
turns.zh: 我们就能让门店重新成为所在领域的领导者，重新投资于我们的经销商，看到它随时间显现的独特价值。在那段时间里，我们在显著改善盈利的同时巩固了渠道，靠的是销量增长，而不是财务工程。

turns.en: What did you see from going into the company to help them do that that was different from seeing on paper that they had decreased marketing spend and there was less of a sell-through as a result?
turns.zh: 走进公司去帮他们做到这些，你所看到的，和纸面上看到的他们营销开支下降、动销 (sell-through) 减少有什么不同？

turns.en: Going into business is understanding what are the key drivers? What is influencing management in their decisions and what they're doing? In that situation, their incentives were misaligned. They were focused on how do I retain earnings versus how do I reinvest in the future of the business? It became clear, we need to reinvest in the future. What does that look like? In a business like that, brand is incredibly important,
turns.zh: 走进一家企业，是去理解关键驱动因素是什么，是什么在影响管理层的决策和他们的做法。在那种情况下，激励机制错位了。他们关注的是如何保住利润，而不是如何为业务的未来再投资。答案逐渐清晰：我们必须为未来再投资。那该怎么做？在这样一家业务里，品牌极其重要——

turns.en: getting awareness, visibility, that connection. They had cut brand spending and marketing spend. The second is the store experience. When you walk into a store, what does it feel like from a customer starting with that customer? What does that look like and how can we improve it? Lastly, I would say it's always culture. There's oftentimes in these organizations where they've declined. There's a cultural element that's got off track. In that case, it becomes stagnant.
turns.zh: 认知度、曝光度、那种连接。他们削减了品牌和营销开支。第二是门店体验：当你走进一家店，从顾客出发，那是什么感觉？应该长什么样？我们怎么改进？最后，永远还有文化。在这些已经衰落的公司里，通常有文化上脱了轨的东西。在那种情况下，组织会变得停滞。

turns.en: They were afraid to make decisions. They weren't leaving the building. There was an opportunity to reinvigorate the culture to help support those first two things.
turns.zh: 他们不敢做决定，也不走出办公室。有机会重振文化，来支撑前面那两件事。

turns.en: In that example, what did you learn about what had happened over those 10 years that hadn't been in place before that led to that period of time where you could change the inflection back up?
turns.zh: 在这个例子里，关于那 10 年到底发生了什么、什么东西的缺失导致了那段下滑，而你又能把它重新拐向上，你学到了什么？

turns.en: Going back and understanding and asking questions, why did we do this? Why didn't we do this? What was happening along the way? I find when sometimes you take a step back and look at a 10-year period, you can see stuff that each year you don't see. When you're looking at a business each year, the little decline, a little decline, maybe it was the market, maybe it was some conditions, maybe it was an anomaly. You don't take ownership of a decline. When you look over 10 years,
turns.zh: 回到原点，理解并提出问题：我们为什么这么做？为什么没这么做？一路发生了什么？我发现，有时候你退后一步看 10 年，能看到每一年单独看时看不到的东西。当你一年一年地看一家公司，小滑坡、又一个滑坡，也许是市场，也许是某种环境，也许被当作异常，没人对下滑承担责任。但当你站在 10 年之外看，

turns.en: your volumes declined 10 plus percent. There's something serious going on here. Then you start to dig in and say, why is that happening? Looking at those next level, and you can look at others in the market. Sherman Williams had done a great job during this time period as an example.
turns.zh: 销量下滑了超过 10%，这里一定有严重的问题。然后你开始深挖为什么，看下一层原因，也可以看市场上的其他人。比如那段时间 Sherwin-Williams 就做得非常出色。

turns.en: What do we need to go figure out to improve that? In this case, the incentives were misaligned. They had focused on the wrong part of the dealer in the relationship and the experience.
turns.zh: 我们需要搞明白什么才能改进？在这个案例里，激励机制错位了，他们把重心放在了经销商关系和体验的错误那一端。

turns.en: They felt like the dealer was waning. They started shifting away from the dealer instead of leaning into the dealer. They were exploring other partnerships with big boxes at the time, and that wasn't the right strategy for this brand, helping coming in, re-centering, refocusing. Usually the answer is in the building. People know what needs to be done and how to do it. Either you're not getting to it or you're not listening to it, or something else is influencing
turns.zh: 他们觉得经销商在衰落，于是开始远离经销商，而不是深耕经销商；当时还在探索与大卖场 (big box) 的合作——那对这个品牌来说不是正确的战略。我们进去帮助重新校准、重新聚焦。通常答案就在企业内部。人们知道该做什么、该怎么做，要么是没去做，要么是没人听他们的，要么是别的东西在影响

turns.en: the decisions that's leading to the wrong outcome. When you look at that example in the context of everything you did at Berkshire, how did you think about managing your time? Warren always said, if you want something done, give it to a busy person. It'll get done over time. I took on more and more. I started on the investing side, became chair of each of these businesses, kept those roles when I became CEO of Pampered Chef, wanted to go get operating experience.
turns.zh: 决策，导致错误的结果。把你在那个例子里的所做，和你在 Berkshire 做的一切放在一起看，你是怎么思考时间管理的？Warren 总说，想找人把事做成，就交给忙人，假以时日一定能做成。我接的事越来越多：从投资开始，兼任这些业务的主席，当 Pampered Chef 的 CEO 时还保留着这些角色——我想去获得运营经验。

turns.en: When you're doing a lot, you start to realize what's most critical, how do you prioritize, and how do you focus? That ends up being what's most interesting. Usually there's three to four things that matter, and we get stuck doing all of these different things. The same thing goes with an investment. There's three or four things that matter. We have a 100-page deck that goes through all these other items, but if you know those three to four things, you spend your time
turns.zh: 当你同时做很多事，你开始意识到什么最关键、怎么排优先级、怎么聚焦。最终那些才是最要紧的。通常只有三四件事真正重要，我们却陷在各种各样的事情里。投资也一样，只有三四件事重要。我们有一份 100 页的文件把所有项目过一遍，但如果你知道那三四件事，把时间花在它们上面，把它们做对，

turns.en: on those and you can get them right. Likelihood that you're successful is much greater, with time is focusing on the things that matter most that are going to move the needle.
turns.zh: 你成功的概率就会大得多——把时间花在最重要的、最能撬动结果的事情上。

turns.en: How about the distinction in your time from being chairman of several companies and then CEO at Pampered Chef? When I was chair, what I realized was there is this opportunity to help management teams and support them, but if you've never been in the shoes, you're always a step behind. You needed to drive real earnings growth in businesses. If I could go be a CEO and get that operating experience, I would have more experience that would help me in the future
turns.zh: 从兼任几家公司的主席，到当 Pampered Chef 的 CEO，那段经历的差别是什么？当我做主席的时候，我意识到可以帮助和支持管理团队，但如果你从来没亲自上过场，你永远慢一拍。企业要真正驱动利润增长。如果我能去当 CEO 拿到运营经验，未来无论做投资还是和管理团队合作，我都会更有底气。

turns.en: with investing or working with management teams. I went to Warren and said, I like to be CEO of Pampered Chef, which I was working with at the time. What I saw was there's a lot of opportunity in that business. It had a strong brand. It had a strong channel. It had been under managed.
turns.zh: 我去找 Warren 说，我想当 Pampered Chef 的 CEO——当时我正在服务这家公司。我看到这个业务有很多机会：品牌强、渠道强，但管理不足。

turns.en: The transition from chairman to CEO was, for a lot of people, surprising. seldom do you see investors go into operating roles. I felt like the future of investing was going to be operating.
turns.zh: 从董事长到 CEO 的转变，对很多人来说很意外，投资人去做运营角色很少见。我觉得投资的未来就在于运营。

turns.en: I would be a much better investor if I went and got that experience directly, gain that credibility, the empathy, the connection with these leaders that would resonate with sellers in the future, resonate with management teams.
turns.zh: 如果我亲自去获得那种经验，我会成为一个好得多的投资人——赢得那种可信度、同理心、与这些领导者之间的连接，未来能与卖方共鸣、与管理团队共鸣。

turns.en: As you look at those different connections with the company from investor to chairman to CEO, how did you think about going in for the first time, communicating what a plan would be?
turns.zh: 从投资人到董事长再到 CEO，你和公司有不同的关系。第一次进去时，你是怎么思考沟通一个计划的？

turns.en: The best way to go in is to go in open mind with more questions than answers. Investors usually come in with answers. Here's our 90-day plan. This is what we're going to go do.
turns.zh: 最好的进去方式是带着开放的心态，问题多于答案。投资人往往带着答案进去：这是我们的 90 天计划，我们要去做这些。

turns.en: You don't actually get the best outcomes in doing that. We started Canberra with Listen and Learning. How do you listen to people in the organization? How do you understand what's going on?
turns.zh: 那样其实得不到最好的结果。我们做 Canvas，是从倾听和学习 (listen and learn) 开始的。你怎么倾听组织里的人？怎么理解正在发生什么？

turns.en: How do you ask the questions that are going to help you be smarter, but also further the conversation? If you do that well, you'll get to a better outcome. You can co-create something that's meaningful in terms of the strategy and the direction and the focus. That is far more powerful than coming in with a plan or a direction.
turns.zh: 怎么提出那些既能让你更聪明、又能推动对话的问题？如果做好了，你会走向更好的结果。你们可以共同创造一个在战略、方向、专注点上都有意义的东西，那比带着一套计划或方向进去要有力得多。

turns.en: What was different from what you expected of Pampercheff? When I came in, I had been working with the business for about a year. I'd spent time learning, listening. I had a strong view at that stage of what we needed to go do.
turns.zh: Pampered Chef 有什么和你预期不同的地方？我进来之前已经和这家公司共事了大约一年，花时间学习、倾听，在那个阶段对我们要做什么已经有很明确的看法。

turns.en: I told Warren, it would take me a year or maybe two years to get this thing coming. It had been in decline for about a decade. It was a big turnaround that I needed to go do.
turns.zh: 我跟 Warren 说，我需要一年、也许两年才能让这个业务好起来。它已经下滑了大约十年，那是我必须去完成的一次大转型。

turns.en: It ended up taking nearly four years to do it. Everything is harder and operating than it seems. Even though I knew what needed to be done, I had the strategy in my mind. I knew I needed to go get the people on board, build the culture. It's a lot harder than you expect because it's all involved people. People are tough. You hire the wrong people. You've got to change them out.
turns.zh: 结果最后花了将近四年。做运营，一切比看起来更难。尽管我知道该做什么，战略在我脑子里，我知道要去让大家上船、去建设文化，但这比想象中难得多，因为全都关系到人。人是难的。你招错人，就得换人。

turns.en: Or you've got to work on culture and retention, which doesn't get changed overnight if you've had challenges in the past. You've got to go invest in people getting up to speed, learning new tools, new practices, new spaces. You've got to build all of this together. That was a huge surprise, humbling, probably not dissimilar from how most investors think.
turns.zh: 或者你得在文化和留任上下功夫——如果过去就有问题，那不是一夜能改的。你得去投入，让员工进入状态，学习新工具、新做法、新领域，这一切都得一起搭建起来。那是一次巨大的意外，让人谦卑，可能和多数投资人的想法没什么两样。

turns.en: Let's take margins from 10% to 14%. That's one click in my spreadsheet. In reality, in a business, that takes a lot more work to do. There's a lot of missteps and mistakes and learnings along the way to get to there.
turns.zh: 我们说把利润率从 10% 拉到 14%，那只是我表格里的一次点击。现实中，在一家企业里，那要付出多得多的工作，一路上有很多失误、错误和学习。

turns.en: Did you progress? You spend this time as a CEO. You could imagine being at Berkshire for a career, going in and working with different companies, larger companies.
turns.zh: 进展如何？你做了这么长时间的 CEO，完全可以想象在 Berkshire 待一辈子，去不同的、更大的公司里工作。

turns.en: At what point in time did you decide you wanted to go do your own thing instead of doing it within Berkshire? I was nearing the conclusion of the turnaround at Pampered Chef. We had the business in a good place. I had met my now co-founder, Brian Humphrey. He had joined me as CFO there.
turns.zh: 你是在什么时候决定要自己出来干，而不只是在 Berkshire 体系内做事的？我当时临近 Pampered Chef 转型的收尾，业务已经处于不错的状态。我也遇到了我现在的联合创始人 Brian Humphrey，他加入那里担任 CFO。

turns.en: We were aligned from a vision and values perspective. I could be at Berkshire forever. I'd have an amazing time there. It's a remarkable company. There's nothing like it, and I don't think there ever will be. It was getting big in terms of capital.
turns.zh: 我们在愿景和价值观上高度契合。我可以永远待在 Berkshire，会非常开心——那是一家了不起的公司，独一无二，我想也永远不会再有第二家。但它在资本规模上越来越大，

turns.en: It had $150 billion in cash at the time. Now it's $300 billion plus. It's hard to move the needle with that size of check. What Berkshire had done 30 or 40 years ago was more interesting to me.
turns.zh: 当时有 1,500 亿美元现金，现在是 3,000 多亿美元。支票开到那个规模，就很难撬动结果了。Berkshire 在 30 年、40 年前做的那些事反而更让我心动。

turns.en: Buying businesses like Benjamin Moore, where you could partner with them, help them accelerate the growth. What I'd seen in the market at the time was there was a growing group of families and founders who wanted something different. They didn't want to sell the traditional private equity. They wanted a Berkshire-like home, but they were just too small. There was this opportunity in that moment to build something that was unique and different, that was solving a pain point.
turns.zh: 买像 Benjamin Moore 那样的企业，与它们合伙、帮它们加速增长。我当时在市场上看到的是，有一群越来越多的家族和创始人想要不一样的东西。他们不想卖给传统私募股权，他们想要一个 Berkshire 式的归宿，但规模又太小。彼时正是机会，去构建独特而不同的、解决痛点的东西。

turns.en: Yes, I could stay here and be happy forever. There's also this opportunity to build something special and unique that was differentiated in the moment.
turns.zh: 没错，我可以留下来，永远开心。但这也是一个机会，去打造一个有差异化、独特而特别的事业。

turns.en: When Brian and you decided you were going to do this, what did you lay out as the core tenets of your philosophy having pulled from your experience as a Berkshire?
turns.zh: 你和 Brian 决定做这件事的时候，基于你们在 Berkshire 的经历，你们奠定了哪些核心信条？

turns.en: There were a few things that resonated with us that were important. One is long-term thinking and a long-term structure. Oftentimes, long-term thinking conflicts with structure. Having those two things together was important to us, and that was paramount to Berkshire, something we wanted to replicate at Canberra. Second was providing that operating lens and that operating expertise.
turns.zh: 有几件事对我们非常重要。一是长期思考加上长期结构——长期思考常常与结构冲突，把两者结合在一起对我们至关重要，这也是 Berkshire 最重要的东西，我们想在 Canvas 复制它。第二是提供运营的视角和运营的专业能力。

turns.en: We had built what is now the Canberra business system from the ground up, learning from greats Dana Hearn, Marmin, and Toyota, Transtime, and others, taking those, applying them for mid-sized companies. Lastly was this partnership mindset, working with families and founders and coming alongside them. So much in traditional private equity is you get told what to do or go drive this or hit this plan versus how do we co-create, build something special and unique.
turns.zh: 我们从零打造了现在的 Canvas 业务系统 (business system)，向 Danaher、Marmin、Toyota、Transtime 等高手学习，把它们应用到中型公司。最后是合伙人心态——与家族和创始人一起工作，站到他们身边。传统私募股权里太多是你被命令去做什么、去达成哪个计划，而我们关注的是如何共同创造、打造独特而特别的东西。

turns.en: That partnership mentality is core and critical to how we operate. What did you do different structurally from the way private equity traditionally runs?
turns.zh: 那种合伙人心态是我们运营方式的核心，也至关重要。那在结构上，你们和传统私募股权的做法有什么不同？

turns.en: We did a longer-term structure. We have 15-plus years in our structure. The benefit of that is it self-selects investors who are long-term oriented, which is beneficial. It's unique for owners who say, look, I'm concerned with the three to four-year treadmill of private equity.
turns.zh: 我们用了更长期的结构，我们的基金期限在 15 年以上。好处是它会自我筛选出真正长期导向的投资者，这很有价值。对那些说我很担心私募股权三四年转手一轮的业主来说，它是独特的。

turns.en: It gives them comfort that their business isn't going to be bought and sold and bought and sold. It's that longer-term horizon that allows our management teams to focus on how do I build this business for decades, not how do I build this business for a quick flip.
turns.zh: 这让他们安心：他们的企业不会一再被买进卖出。正是那个更长的周期，让我们的管理团队能专注于如何把企业建成能持续几十年的事业，而不是如何快速做高再卖掉。

turns.en: What do you find when you went into the market with that structure? From an investor perspective, there's some investors it isn't a fit for. It doesn't match their structure, their duration, their liquidity needs, which we understand.
turns.zh: 带着这个结构走进市场，你们发现了什么？从投资者角度，有些投资者不匹配——和他们的结构、久期、流动性需求不合，这我们能理解。

turns.en: There was a group of investors where immediately resonated with them. It was aligned with how they think about building businesses. A lot of our businesses will generate a fair amount of cash because they don't have a lot of leverage. We can return capital. We have a business JM test. We've owned it three years.
turns.zh: 但也有一群投资者立刻产生了共鸣，这和他们对做企业的理解完全一致。我们的很多企业杠杆不高，会产生大量现金，我们可以返还资本。比如 JM Test，我们已经持有它三年。

turns.en: We forexed the earnings in the business over that period and returned our initial capital to investors. We still own our 70% plus of the business. That is a great model where, yes, there's liquidity. It's not the same as an exit. We'd rather continue to own that business than back to it.
turns.zh: 这段时间里，我们用公司的利润自由现金流 (free cash flow) 把初始资本全部返还给了投资者，同时仍然持有这家企业 70% 以上的股份。这是一个很好的模式——是的，它提供了流动性，虽然不等于退出。相比于卖掉，我们更愿意继续持有这家企业。

turns.en: How did you encapsulate that idea of partnership? There's a few things that we highlight. Structure is important, but it's one part of the three-legged stool. There's a long-term structure that allows us to invest in these high-quality businesses. There's our Canberra community, which is how we get to know companies.
turns.zh: 你们怎么概括合伙这个理念？有几件事。结构很重要，但它只是三腿凳 (three-legged stool) 中的一条腿。长期结构让我们投资这些高质量企业；Canvas 社群 (community) 是我们认识公司的方式——

turns.en: We build relationships over the long term. There's the business system as we add value. They all get mutually reinforced and powerful together. By having that longer-term structure, our management teams can think longer-term. By our management teams thinking longer-term, we can drive above-average returns. By having our Canberra business system, we can use it in our community. By having that in our community, we get to know owners and CEOs well ahead of any
turns.zh: 我们长期建立关系；还有业务系统，这是我们创造价值的方式。三者相互增强，合在一起才有力量。有了长期结构，管理团队能看得更远；管理团队看得更远，我们能驱动高于平均的回报；有 Canvas 业务系统，我们可以把它用于社群；通过社群，我们在任何潜在合伙

turns.en: potential partnership. When those things start to compound on each other, you get the value of it. It has been tough to communicate that story because it's not a simple, easy one.
turns.zh: 开始之前很久就认识业主和 CEO。当这些东西开始相互叠加时，你就得到了它的价值。因为这不是一个简单直白的故事，把它讲清楚一直很难。

turns.en: Our belief and our competitive advantage is those things. That becomes stronger and stronger over time and harder for someone else to come in and replicate. The most powerful part of the story, though, is seeing it in the results. When we started a few years ago, it was a much harder message to get it out there and able to communicate because it was a vision of what we were building.
turns.zh: 我们的信念和竞争优势就在于此，它随时间越来越强，也越来越难被别人复制。但最有说服力的还是在结果中看到它。几年前刚开始的时候，那还只是我们正在打造的愿景，很难向外传达。

turns.en: It wasn't yet to come. You mentioned the Canberra community. What did you build to generate that community? When I started as CEO of Pampere Chef, it was lonely. I had to go out and meet with owners, meet with other executives to understand how do you manage a business effectively and well.
turns.zh: 它还没兑现。你提到了 Canvas 社群，你们建了什么来创造这个社群？我刚当 Pampered Chef 的 CEO 时很孤独。我得出去见各种业主、其他高管，学习怎么把企业管好。

turns.en: When I was doing that, I thought, wow, it would be so great to have a resource. Someone who could come alongside me and say, this is what a great strategic planning process looks like or this is how you can improve your executive hiring skills. When I started that journey, I realized there was this need to help owners. They wanted to learn and grow and CEOs in particular.
turns.zh: 在那段日子里我就想：要是有一个资源就好了，能有人站在我身边说：好的战略规划流程长这样，或者你可以这样提升招聘高管的能力。当我开始那段旅程时，我意识到帮助业主是一种真实的需求，他们想学习和成长，尤其是 CEO。

turns.en: So when we started Canberra, we brought that idea forward with this opportunity to get to know owners and CEOs over time. We built the Canberra community to be that home that we wanted to have in terms of learning and growing together. Now we have 4,000 CEOs in the community and owners and C-suite executives where we're helping them with their business, taking a step back and saying, this is what a great KPI process looks like. These are what the best benchmarks are.
turns.zh: 所以当我们创办 Canvas 时，我们把那个想法推进下来，借这个契机长期认识业主和 CEO。我们打造 Canvas 社群，就是当年我们自己想要的那种共同学习、共同成长的归宿。现在社群里有 4,000 名 CEO、业主和高管层，我们帮他们经营企业，退后一步告诉他们：好的 KPI 流程应该长这样，这些是最好的基准。

turns.en: That community relationship has been powerful and helpful for us. We learn about new spaces. We get to know businesses. Most importantly, these companies get to know us.
turns.zh: 这层社群关系对我们既强大又有帮助。我们了解新的领域，认识各种企业，最重要的是，这些企业也在认识我们。

turns.en: We build trust and credibility. All of our investments have come through direct relationships. Four of our seven have come through the community. We're building goodwill. We're building trust.
turns.zh: 我们建立信任和信誉。我们所有的投资都来自直接关系，七家里有四家来自社群。我们在积累商誉、积累信任。

turns.en: Even if the companies aren't ever going to take a partner or not interested in a partner, what we find is they become great ambassadors for us. They share about Canberra with their friends, other CEOs, and that's been powerful. How do you get from zero to 4,000?
turns.zh: 即使有些企业永远不会考虑找合伙人，我们发现它们会成为我们很棒的大使——它们向朋友、其他 CEO 分享 Canvas，这种力量很可观。你们是怎么从 0 做到 4,000 的？

turns.en: We started with our first program. It's called Build with Canberra. CEOs apply to it. In our first cohort, we had five CEOs we selected. Those first five CEOs recommended other CEOs.
turns.zh: 我们从第一个项目开始，叫 Build with Canvas，CEO 申请加入。第一届我们选了 5 位 CEO，这第一批 CEO 推荐了更多 CEO，

turns.en: We went out to our network and started inviting them. At the end of our first year in 2021, we had 127 CEOs. It was still nascent at that stage. We went from 127 to 500 to 1,000 to 2 to 3.
turns.zh: 我们再向我们的网络发出邀请。2021 年第一年结束时，我们有 127 位 CEO，那个阶段还很稚嫩。然后从 127 到 500，到 1,000，到 2,000、3,000。

turns.en: When you add value, it becomes more of a referral community where people are inviting other people. Now we've extended the programs. We have that three-month program. We also have a three-week masterclass where you can go deep on hiring. We'll do three 90-minute sessions and help you in hiring. We have webinars every month on different topics. We just did one on mission critical roles. We started doing local and national events where we bring people together in
turns.zh: 当你持续创造价值，它就越来越像一个转介绍社群，人们邀请其他人。现在我们扩展了项目：除了三个月的项目，还有三周的精修班 (masterclass)，可以深入学招聘——三场 90 分钟的课帮你把招聘做好。我们每个月都有不同主题的线上研讨会，刚做了一场讲关键岗位的。我们开始做本地和全国活动，把人们聚在

turns.en: different communities in person so they can connect with other leaders in their regions or in their areas. That has become more of a compounding nature where the relationships become stronger. Our connections become more powerful. We get to build this trust with these individuals. It's been a journey. It's been amazing to see the power of that, how many people engage in it, how much they share, and bring other people into the community. What's the breadth
turns.zh: 不同的社区线下面对面，让他们和本地区、本领域的其他领导者建立连接。这件事开始有复利的味道——关系越来越强，连接越来越有力，我们和这些人建立起信任。这是一段旅程。看到它的力量、看到多少人参与、多少分享、把多少人带进社群，真的非常奇妙。你们通过社群给这些 CEO 传授的内容有多宽？

turns.en: of what you've taught to these CEOs through the community? We start with our business system, which is focused on how do you manage a mid-size company? It starts with people. How do you attract, develop, and engage talent? Everything from mission critical roles in hiring to talent engagement, communications, town halls to incentive plans, talent development, career planning, career mapping, those types of conversations. Then we have the operating system,
turns.zh: 我们从业务系统开始，它聚焦于如何经营一家中型公司。起点是人：如何吸引、培养、激发人才——从关键岗位与招聘，到人才敬业度、沟通、员工大会，到激励计划、人才培养、职业规划、职业地图这类话题。然后是运营系统，

turns.en: which falls into how do you build a plan? What's your strategy? How do you resource that plan? How do you think about capital allocation? How do you think about KPIs, budgeting, all of those dynamics, and how you manage a business? Then we have operational excellence.
turns.zh: 包括怎么做计划、战略是什么、怎么为计划配置资源、怎么思考资本配置、KPI、预算，以及管理企业的种种维度。再就是运营卓越 (operational excellence)：

turns.en: How do you continually get better and have better use of your assets, your costs, anything that you have supporting the business, and then growth? Where's the growth in your business and what does that look like? That's the core of where we spend our time. That helps probably 80% plus of companies.
turns.zh: 如何持续变得更好，更高效地使用你的资产、成本，以及一切支撑业务的东西。然后是增长：你的增长在哪里，长什么样？这是我们花时间最集中的核心，能帮到 80% 以上的公司。

turns.en: They struggle with topics within that. Each business is different. For one, it might be hiring. For another, it might be KPIs. We're helping them in that. There's other topics we've expanded out by demand. How do I think about M&A? How do I think about developing a board? How do I think about AI? How do I think about tariffs? We've led roundtable sessions as those topics come up.
turns.zh: 他们的问题几乎都在这些范围之内。每家企业不一样：这家可能是招聘，那家可能是 KPI，我们在这些方面帮他们。还有一些按需求扩展出来的话题：怎么看待并购 (M&A)？怎么组建董事会？怎么思考 AI？怎么思考关税？话题出现时，我们会组织圆桌。

turns.en: We're sharing our own experience and perspectives, but we're also getting best practices and learnings across the cohort and across the group. We learn a lot with people who are at the forefront of what they're doing in their industry or on a specific topic. How have you nurtured and cultivated the community once you've built it to that many people to make sure that people stay engaged?
turns.zh: 我们分享自己的经验和视角，同时也在同期学员和整个社群里收获最佳实践与经验。我们从那些在行业或特定主题上处于最前沿的人身上学到很多。社群做到这么多人规模后，你们怎么持续培育它、让大家保持参与？

turns.en: Every month, we put a written brief out on topics that we're covering that we think are helpful. The sessions that we're hosting virtually and in person that have those touch points.
turns.zh: 每个月我们会就认为有帮助的在讲主题发布书面简报。我们有线上和线下的活动，那些都是触点。

turns.en: Beyond that, it's those personal touches. We're thinking about you. You told us you were focused on hiring and that was a tough challenge. Here's some new material as it relates to that.
turns.zh: 除此之外，还有个性化的连接：我们记着你——你说过你正在为招聘头疼，那是个难题，这里有一些相关的新材料。

turns.en: Understanding where people are, touching base with them and connecting. Everyone is struggling with something different in their business. As we get to know them, we can be more helpful in doing that. Making connections might be you're looking for a board member in this space. We have five community members in that space who might be potential board members or know someone.
turns.zh: 理解每个人所处的位置，和他们保持联系、建立连接。每个人在自己的企业里应对的难题都不同，我们越了解他们，就能帮得越准。连接也可能是这样的：你在找一个某个领域的董事，我们社群里有五位成员在这个领域，可能适合当董事，或者认识合适的人。

turns.en: Facilitating those introductions, connections, strengthens the power of the community. There's a small firm. How do you scale your resources to be able to deliver that type of customized experience across so many people? It's everyone's job to help support the community, participate in events and what we're doing. It's core to how we operate and how we think.
turns.zh: 促成这些引荐和连接，会让社群的力量更强。你们是一家小公司，怎么扩展资源，为这么多人提供这种定制化体验？支持社群是每个人的工作，参与活动、参与我们在做的事。它融入我们的运营和思维方式。

turns.en: That becomes second nature to everyone and what we're doing. Then we're thoughtful about how to do it. We're going to be focused. Once we build the muscle, it becomes easier and it becomes more scalable. Build with Canberra, the first program we launched five years ago. We constantly improve it. The core stays the same. If we have a new cohort and new members, we're not changing everything constantly. That allows us to scale and add on specific programs and initiatives that
turns.zh: 对每个人来说，这成了第二天性。我们在方法上很用心，会保持专注。一旦肌肉建立起来，事情就更容易、更可规模化。Build with Canvas 是我们五年前启动的第一个项目，我们不断打磨它，内核不变。如果有新的同期班和新成员，我们不会天翻地覆地改，这让我们能规模化，同时叠加特定的项目和举措，

turns.en: are meeting our leaders and our CEOs where they are. I'd love to turn to how you leverage that into your investing. You have all these people now in your network. What have you decided that you're looking for of the companies that you may want to buy? We start off big picture on what we're looking for, which is industrial services, manufacturing, some consumer. We're focused on high-quality businesses. We're looking at businesses that are five to 50 million in earnings.
turns.zh: 去贴合我们的领导者和 CEO 当下的状态。我很想聊聊你们如何把这一切转化到投资上。你网络里有这么多人了，对于你们想收购的公司，定了哪些标准？我们先从大的方向说起：工业服务、制造、一些消费。我们专注高质量企业，看利润在 500 万到 5,000 万美元之间的公司。

turns.en: What's most important is the business model. Does it have a moat? Does it have a competitive advantage? Can we see it quantitatively? Qualitatively can re-understand what's happening with that moat. That's what we're focused on and what we're looking for. Anyone can join the community who has a business over 10 million in revenue. A CEO of 10 million in revenue can join. By doing that, we have a lot of people who aren't in our target space or what we're looking for and we're completely
turns.zh: 最重要的是商业模式。有没有护城河 (moat)？有没有竞争优势？能量化地看到吗？定性上能否重新理解这条护城河正在发生什么？这就是我们关注和寻找的。任何收入超过 1,000 万美元公司的 CEO 都可以加入社群。正因如此，社群里有很多并不在我们目标范围或我们寻找方向上的人，我们非常乐意

turns.en: happy to have them join the community. With the people that we get to know and that are interested in their businesses or they're interested in a potential partner, we spend more and more time with them. The days of auctions, it's transactional. It's not how most people think about their businesses. If you've built your business over decades or it's a family business or your founder, the idea of selling it through an auction doesn't resonate with a lot of people. You
turns.zh: 让他们加入社群。在我们认识的人里，那些对我们有意、或他们的企业有潜在合伙可能的，我们花越来越多的时间相处。拍卖式交易的那一套是纯交易式的，不是大多数人看待自己企业的方式。如果你的企业是几十年做出来的，或者是家族企业，或者你是创始人，把它拿到拍卖会上卖掉这件事，对很多人根本没有共鸣。你

turns.en: care about your employees. You care about the future of your business. Price is important, but it may not be the only thing that's important to you. It's the future value creation, your legacy, how you're going to focus on customers. The relationships we're building to the community we think are more powerful and over time, how more businesses will be transacted will be through those relationships versus a traditional auction process.
turns.zh: 在意你的员工，在意企业的未来。价格重要，但未必是唯一重要的。是未来的价值创造、你的传承、你打算怎么继续服务客户。我们相信这些通过社群建立的关系更有力量，而且随着时间推移，越来越多的企业交易将通过这些关系达成，而不是传统的拍卖流程。

turns.en: We're going to take a quick break in the action to tell you about Brookfield. Brookfield invests in the thing behind the thing behind the next big thing. Their focus across infrastructure, energy, real estate, private equity and credit is helping to build the backbone of the global economy. Brookfield combines deep operational expertise with disciplined long-term investing, uncovering value and partnering alongside clients to shape
turns.zh: 节目中间我们插播一下，给你介绍 Brookfield。Brookfield 投资于大事件背后、再背后的事物。他们在基础设施、能源、房地产、私募股权和信贷领域的布局，正在帮助构建全球经济的骨架。Brookfield 把深厚的运营专长与纪律严明的长期投资结合起来，与客户并肩挖掘价值、塑造

turns.en: tomorrow's economy today. Invest in the businesses that shape tomorrow. Learn how you can own what's next at Brookfield.com slash own. This is not an offer to sell or investment advice. Investing involves risk, including the loss of capital. And now back to the show. What are your favorite metrics on assessing a business, the quality of the business or the mode?
turns.zh: 明天的经济于今日。投资那些塑造明天的企业，到 brookfield.com/own 了解如何拥有未来。这不构成出售要约，也不是投资建议。投资有风险，包括本金损失。现在回到节目。你们评估一家企业、评估企业质量或护城河时，最看重的指标是什么？

turns.en: We look at a return on invested capital and other derivatives of that. Then we try to see over time are those returns and capital going up, going down, staying the same? Qualitatively, can we understand why? What is the mode? Is it brand and channel? Is it network effect, niche scale? Is it route density? Do we think that's going to get better over time, worse over time or stay the same? And that qualitative assessment is important in understanding
turns.zh: 我们看投入资本回报率 (return on invested capital) 及其衍生指标。然后我们试图看到，这些资本回报随时间是上升、下降还是持平？定性上，我们能否理解为什么？护城河是什么？是品牌加渠道，还是网络效应、利基规模 (niche scale)、线路密度 (route density)？我们觉得它会随时间变好、变差还是不变？这种定性评估对于理解

turns.en: the overall quality of the business, what the potential future path might be. How about assessing management? We look at five M's. Moat is one, market's the second, third is management, fourth's more potential and then last, margin of safety.
turns.zh: 企业的整体质量和潜在的未来路径很重要。那你们怎么评估管理层？我们看五个 M：Moat（护城河）是第一，Market（市场）是第二，第三是 Management（管理层），第四是 More potential（更多潜力），最后是 Margin of safety（安全边际）。

turns.en: On the management, what we're trying to see is, do they have a track record of success? Do they have strong integrity? Do they care about the business? Are they there for the right reasons? Do they have a view on the future of the strategy, the company and what does it look like?
turns.zh: 关于管理层，我们想看的是：他们有没有成功的履历？有没有很强的正直感？在不在意这家企业？他们是出于正确的原因在这里吗？他们对未来、对战略、对公司有没有看法，那个图景是什么样的？

turns.en: There's an opportunity to come help them. But maybe we've done a great job building our business. We think that we need to build out other skill sets or focus on people, revenue or sales that we haven't done before. We come alongside them to help build out that broader framework and team. We're trying to assess how strong have they delivered, how strong are they from a character integrity perspective as well.
turns.zh: 有时候机会在于我们过来帮忙。比如他们把自己的企业建设得很出色，但觉得需要补上其他技能，或者要拓展以前没做过的人才、营收或销售领域，我们就站到他们身边，帮他们搭建更完整的框架和团队。我们试图评估：他们的业绩兑现得有多强，品格和正直方面又有多可靠。

turns.en: In family and businesses, inevitably, you have the family involved. How do you balance a business that you think you like and maybe could be better under your ownership with a family that's been around it for a long time who you may not think is the right long-term leader? We try to understand what's the motivation or the goal of the family and the leaders in the business when we partner. Sometimes it's different. We find about half of our partners are looking
turns.zh: 在家族企业里，家族成员必然牵涉其中。你们怎么平衡——一家你觉得不错、在你们旗下可能做得更好的企业——和一个陪伴企业很久、但你可能认为不适合做长期领导者的家族？我们试图理解家族和企业管理层的动机或目标是什么。有时不一样。我们发现大约一半的合伙人在找

turns.en: for a successor. They want someone to come in and help them in this next phase of growth right away or in three to five years. They don't have a successor in the business.
turns.zh: 接班人——他们希望有人进来，立刻或三到五年内在下一个增长阶段帮他们，而企业内部没有接班人。

turns.en: That's a common trend among a lot of baby boomers. The second profile is typically someone who's a builder, a founder or maybe second, third generation. They want to build their company, take it to the next level, but they want someone to come alongside them and help them.
turns.zh: 这在很多婴儿潮一代企业家里是个普遍趋势。第二类画像通常是建设者——创始人，或者第二代、第三代，他们想把公司建大、带到下一个层级，但希望有人并肩帮忙。

turns.en: We have both Scott Morrison at JMTest. When we were partnering with them, he wanted a successor or he wanted to transition out over the next few years. Brandon McVaugh at laboratory testing. He was the next generation. He wanted to build and scale. From there, we understand and say, are we aligned in our vision for the business? We try to be really upfront what we think we can build together. If it's not a good fit, we'd rather acknowledge that
turns.zh: 这两种我们都有。比如 JM Test 的 Scott Morrison，我们洽谈合伙时，他想找接班人，或者想在接下来几年过渡出去。又比如做实验室检测 (laboratory testing) 的 Brandon McVaugh，他是下一代，想建设和扩张。在此基础上，我们去理解并问：我们对企业的愿景一致吗？我们会非常坦率地说清楚我们认为一起能建成什么。如果不合适，我们宁愿在交割前承认，

turns.en: and do it before we close versus have these disagreements or uncomfortable conversations post-close. We try to be really transparent of what we're thinking and what it looks like.
turns.zh: 也不要在交割之后出现分歧或难以开口的争执。我们尽量把我们的想法和图景讲透明。

turns.en: Fortunately, we've been aligned with our leaders. We think there's shared vision, shared values, shared concept of what we're going to go build together. That's how we think about the seller profile. Once you've found something that you're excited about, you've had productive conversations with the family. What are some of the deal dynamics of getting one of these deals done?
turns.zh: 幸运的是，我们的领导层都和我们契合，我们认为有共同的愿景、共同的价值观、共同要去建设的图景。这就是我们对卖家画像的思考。一旦你发现一家令你兴奋的企业、也和家人进行了富有成效的对话，做成这样一笔交易，交易动态是什么样的？

turns.en: We usually start off with what's important to you and a partner. What are you looking for? Trying to understand what they're thinking about in that space. In that comes out a lot.
turns.zh: 我们通常从什么对你和合伙人重要开始问：你在找什么？试图理解他们在这个问题上的想法，很多信息就会浮出水面。

turns.en: I care about the headline value today. I care about my future value creation. I want to retain a stake or I want to make sure my team members are protected. They're in a good place, understanding what that looks like is important. We usually ask our owners what they think about valuation.
turns.zh: 比如我在意今天的估值数字，我在意未来的价值创造，我想保留一部分股权，或者我想确保我的团队成员受到保护、处于好的位置。理解这些诉求很重要。我们通常会先问业主，他们觉得估值应该是多少。

turns.en: They know the business better than we do. What do they think is fair and reasonable? Sometimes we're not in the ballpark. It's different than what we think.
turns.zh: 他们比我们更了解这家企业。他们觉得什么是公平合理的？有时候我们连 ballpark 都不挨着——和我们的想法不一样。

turns.en: It allows us to start that conversation there. Usually some surprises come up. Maybe the earnings is a little bit different than what they have in their books as we do a quality of earnings, perhaps market conditions change a bit. We just have a conversation. This is your goal and this is our goal. What's a win-win that we can develop? We try to put ourselves in their shoes. If it was our family business, what do we think would be fair and reasonable? That usually gets us to a
turns.zh: 那让我们从那里开始对话。通常过程中会有一些意外：做盈利质量审查 (quality of earnings) 时，盈利可能和他们账上的数据有些不同，或者市场环境变了。我们就摊开聊：这是你的目标，这是我们的目标，什么样的双赢方案可以设计出来？我们试着把自己放到他们的位子上：如果这是我们的家族企业，什么对我们才算公平合理？那通常能把我们带到

turns.en: place where we can have an attractive structure. That is a win-win for both of us. We're solving the needs real time as we go versus a traditional auction process is you don't talk that much with management. You don't understand. There's 10 other people in the process. You're putting forth your best bid, but you can't work through the nuances. You don't get to the best structure, the best alignment in those situations. We think it's more effective to be able to understand what their
turns.zh: 一个有吸引力的结构上，对我们双方都是双赢。我们实时解决彼此的需求，而不像传统拍卖流程——你和管理团队聊得不多，不了解情况，流程里还有 10 个别的买家，你出最好的价，却没法打磨细节，那种情况下你拿不到最好的结构、最好的对齐。我们认为，先理解他们的需求，

turns.en: needs are and then structure something that works mutually for both parties. How do you manage around the inevitable family dynamics that might come up, even if you think you're aligned with the people on the outside too?
turns.zh: 然后构造一个对双方都成立的方案，更有效。即便你觉得和外面的人都对齐了，家族内部不可避免的动态，你们怎么应对？

turns.en: We try to take it with a transparency, trust, and honest conversation about situations. There's surprises that come up. We've got all these family members in the business. Some are working. Some aren't working. We have a lot of people married. There's all these dynamics that come up. We try to be reasonable to say, what would we do if we were on the other side? What might be an issue and what might not be? Family businesses are special because the people in
turns.zh: 我们试着用透明、信任和就事论事的坦诚对话来处理。总会有意外冒出来：家族里的人都在企业里，有的在职、有的不在，还有大量姻亲，各种动态都会出现。我们试着通情达理地想：如果我们在对面那一侧，会怎么做？什么会是问题，什么不会？家族企业很特别，因为在企业里的这些人往往从小在其中长大，他们知道太多，

turns.en: the business usually have grown up in it. They know so much. They have this depth of understanding and knowledge. We want to reward that and support that when we find it. We also recognize when there's gaps or issues. At JMTest, Brad Morrison, who was third generation, he was a director in the business, doing a great job. We met him and he's remarkable. We're going to promote him to COO. We want to enhance his leadership in the business. There's other situations where you
turns.zh: 有那种深度的理解和积累。当我们看到这种价值时，我们想奖励和支持它；当存在差距或问题时，我们也会承认。比如在 JM Test，第三代的 Brad Morrison 是企业的董事，干得很出色。我们认识他之后觉得他非常优秀，要把他提升为 COO，加强他在企业里的领导力。也有另一种情况：你见到企业里的家族成员，

turns.en: meet family members in the business and they're not the right fit. You've got to have that conversation of, I know you're getting a paycheck, but we're going to transition you out over these months or years if it's not the right fit for the business. Our goals always do what's best for the long-term health of the business. We're going to make the decisions that we think help support that. We're not going to get it right every time. That's our focus. If we focus on
turns.zh: 发现他们并不合适。那就得开口谈：我知道你在领薪水，但如果这个岗位对企业不合适，我们会在几个月或几年里把你过渡出去。我们的目标始终是为企业的长期健康做最好的事，做我们认为有助于它的决定。我们不会每次都做对，但这是我们的方向。如果我们聚焦于什么对公司的长期健康最好，

turns.en: what's best for the long-term health for the company, that's going to ultimately be what's best for employees. That's going to be best for owners and best for investors because we're going to get the best outcomes. That may require some tough decisions along the way.
turns.zh: 那最终对员工也最好，对业主和投资人也最好——因为我们要拿到最好的结果。为此路上可能需要一些艰难的决定。

turns.en: How do you plan for having difficult conversations if there is a family member who you've decided probably isn't the right long-term fit for the business?
turns.zh: 如果你们认定某位家族成员大概不适合长期留在企业，你们怎么准备那场艰难的谈话？

turns.en: With humility, with respect, almost always in person, not getting on a Zoom and saying, Johnny's got to go. We're focused on what's important to the business. How do we approach it with the respect that we would hope someone would approach us and our family businesses?
turns.zh: 带着谦逊，带着尊重，几乎总是当面谈，而不是开个 Zoom 说一句 Johnny 得走人。我们聚焦什么对企业最重要，用我们希望别人对待我们自家企业的那份尊重去沟通。

turns.en: Having that conversation, it's understanding. Coming in with an open mind, sometimes we come in with too many preconceived notions of this won't work or why do they have that. We just ask questions. You've done it this way. Why? What do you think is working well or not working well?
turns.zh: 进行那种对话需要理解，带着开放的心态进来。有时候我们带着太多先入之见——这行不通，或者他们怎么那样做。我们就多问问题：你们一直是这样做的，为什么？你觉得什么有效、什么无效？

turns.en: What do you think we need to do to get better? Oftentimes, we can get there together where it's not us saying something needs to change. It's coming to the realization that maybe this isn't what's best for the business. If that's the case, okay, what are we going to do to address it?
turns.zh: 你觉得我们要怎么改进？很多时候，我们可以一起走到那个认知——不是我们要求改变什么，而是共同意识到，也许现在这样对企业并不是最好的。如果是那样，好，我们该怎么解决？

turns.en: Once you've bought a company, how do you take the plans that you have and roll them out in that first year of ownership? We start with listen and learn. We don't come in with a 90-day plan or we're going to hit these goals. It's understanding what that business needs, asking questions. Are there other similar industries that might be relevant for us to learn from? As we go through that, we work with the management team and co-creating what's our vision through the future.
turns.zh: 一旦你们买下公司，你们怎么把你们的计划落地到第一年？我们从倾听和学习开始，没有 90 天计划，也不是我们要达到这些指标。而是去理解这家企业需要什么，问问题：有没有其他相关行业值得我们学习？在这个过程中，我们和管理团队共创对未来的愿景。

turns.en: What are we building towards? What are our goals? What do we want to go accomplish? What does success look like? Co-creating that, it becomes ours together. It's not Camberx saying this or the management team saying that. It becomes one plan and it's powerful because there's true ownership in the management team. Once we have that established and our Camberx Business System team works closely with the management team and building that,
turns.zh: 我们要建成什么？目标是什么？想达成什么？成功长什么样？共创出来的东西会变成我们共同的，不是 Canvas 说这个、管理团队说那个。它变成一个计划，而且很有力量，因为管理团队真正拥有它。一旦确立之后，Canvas 业务系统团队就与管理团队紧密合作去搭建，

turns.en: then we have the North Star. What's our purpose? What are we going to achieve? What's our strategy to get there? What are our goals associated with it?
turns.zh: 然后就有了北极星 (North Star)：我们的使命是什么？我们要达成什么？通往那里的战略是什么？相关的目标是什么？

turns.en: What plans, KPIs, resources do we need to have to go accomplish that? As you go to implement different aspects of KBS with different companies, I'd love to ask you some of the key things you've found that work well. What do you coach or teach about hiring practices that are effective? We first start any business understanding what are the mission critical roles. Almost every men's size company has 15 to 20 critical roles you need to be successful.
turns.zh: 需要什么样的计划、KPI 和资源去实现它？在不同公司落地业务系统 (KBS) 的不同部分时，很想听你讲讲哪些做法特别有效。你在招聘上会教练或传授什么？任何企业我们都先理解什么是关键岗位 (mission critical roles)。几乎每家中型公司都有 15 到 20 个必须配好的关键岗位才能成功。

turns.en: What are those? What's our talent look like in those roles? Do we have the right people? Do we have the right roles? Do we need to make adjustments? That starts us. Once we do that, there probably are a handful of roles we need to go hire for. How do we create a strong hiring process? We've built ours based on GH Smart, their who process, which we think is single-handedly the best hiring process. We've adapted it for ourselves. We have three components of it. The first is
turns.zh: 它们是什么？这些岗位上我们的人才状况如何？人对不对？岗位对不对？要不要调整？这是我们的起点。之后通常有几个岗位要招人。怎么打造强有力的招聘流程？我们基于 Geoff Smart 的 Who 方法搭建了我们的流程，我们认为是当下最好的招聘流程，并做了自己的改造。它有三个部分。第一是

turns.en: around scorecard. Do you have a clear scorecard of what success looks like? Do you have a mission? Do you have objectives? Do you have outcomes? That, most people skip over. They start a JD and start hiring. That helps us get alignment of what type of leader we need, what type of goals do we need to have to accomplish this, who disagrees with that, get all the stakeholders to get their input in. Once we have the scorecard, then we think about sourcing. Most sourcing is reactive.
turns.zh: 计分卡 (scorecard)：你有没有一张清晰的成功长什么样的计分卡？有没有使命？有没有目标？有没有结果？大多数人跳过这一步，直接写个 JD 就开始招。计分卡帮我们对齐需要什么样的领导者、要达成目标需要什么样的指标，谁有不同意见？把所有相关方的意见收集进来。有了计分卡，接下来是寻源 (sourcing)。大多数寻源是被动的：

turns.en: You post and whoever's available applies. Usually the best people are happily employed. You need to go find them. We spend a lot of time proactively building those relationships, and we focus a lot on our employee value proposition. Why does someone want to join one of our businesses? What are they going to learn? Where are they going to grow? What are they going to gain from that experience, communicating that? Then we focus on selection.
turns.zh: 你发个职位，谁有空谁来投。但通常最好的人都在愉快地就业着，你得主动去找。我们花大量时间主动建立那些关系，并非常强调员工价值主张 (employee value proposition)：一个人为什么要加入我们的企业？他会学到什么、在哪里成长、从这段经历里获得什么——把这些讲清楚。然后是甄选 (selection)，

turns.en: That's where most people spend their time when they think about hiring. It's a combination. There's the interviews. We're structured. We have competency-based interviews, cultural-based interviews, and we have outcomes-based interviews. After that, we do a case study that depth of analysis and understanding how they think, how they operate. We layer in cognitive, behavioral assessments, back-channel references. Most people understand intuitively that this
turns.zh: 这是多数人想到招聘时唯一花时间的地方。我们是组合式的：面试是结构化的，有能力面试、文化面试、结果面试；之后做案例分析，深度理解他们如何思考、如何做事。我们再叠加认知测评、行为测评、非正式的背景参考。大多数人凭直觉知道这些

turns.en: can improve their hiring process. They don't have the discipline and the adherence to it. We find the business system is driving that adherence to a system in a structured way of thinking. If we have that discipline on hiring, we can improve our odds of success.
turns.zh: 能改进招聘流程，但缺乏坚持到底的纪律。我们发现业务系统带来的正是这种对系统、对结构化思考方式的坚持。如果我们在招聘上有这种纪律，就能提高成功的概率。

turns.en: GH Smart estimates that 50% of hires are mistakes. If we can get that improved to 70% of the right hire or 80% or 90%, it's a huge unlock in a mid-sized company where people are everything driving the value of the business. As you're bringing in aspects of the system, metrics, KPIs to a company that hasn't had it before, what does that rollout process look like?
turns.zh: Geoff Smart 估计 50% 的招聘是错误的。如果我们能把正确率提高到 70%、80%、90%，在一家中型公司里就是巨大的释放——人是一切，驱动着企业的价值。当你把系统里的指标、KPI 带给一家从没接触过的公司，落地过程是什么样的？

turns.en: Understanding where they are to start. Some companies are further along on their journey than others. Then it's understanding what are the biggest business drivers. Sometimes we have a sense of them. There's the obvious ones. We need to track revenue or earnings. There's a lot more behind that. Once we understand what the biggest drivers are, then can we get clarity and visibility into them? Then can we drive that throughout the organization? But JMTest as an example, we quickly
turns.zh: 先理解他们的起点，有些公司在旅程上走得更远。然后理解什么是最大的业务驱动因素。有时候我们已有感觉，也有那些显而易见的——需要跟踪营收、盈利，但背后还有更多。一旦理解最大的驱动因素是什么，能不能对它们形成清晰度和可见度？然后能不能把它贯穿到整个组织？以 JM Test 为例，我们很快

turns.en: realized that turnaround time was one of the most critical metrics. At the time, they didn't know their turnaround time at a company, let alone branch or down to the individual. We tried to understand as turnaround time, how do we provide the dashboards, the clarity, the visibility that our team members can understand it? Once we start doing that, then you unlock potential where your entry-level workers or frontline workers can say, I can drive turnaround if I reconfigure my
turns.zh: 意识到周转时间 (turnaround time) 是最关键的指标之一。当时他们连公司层面的周转时间都不知道，更不用说部门或个人层面。我们试图理解：围绕周转时间，怎么提供仪表盘、清晰度和可见度，让我们的团队成员看得懂它？一旦开始这样做，你就释放了潜力——入门级员工或一线员工也能说：如果我重新布置工位、改变这些环节，我就能缩短周转时间。

turns.en: workspace and change these things. Then you get more people thinking about how to drive turnaround time, not just the leadership team. That's when you're starting powerful. Then what we start to do is say, can we align our incentives to those KPIs? If we align our incentives to those KPIs, people have a motivation to do it. Then we start rewarding them. At JMTest, in the first couple of years, our bonuses went up 3x because we had been driving the results and they were seeing it,
turns.zh: 于是思考怎么缩短周转时间的不再只是领导层，而是更多人。这就开始强大了。接下来我们做的是：能不能把激励和这些 KPI 对齐？对齐了，人们就有了动力，然后我们开始兑现奖励。在 JM Test，头两年我们的奖金涨了 3 倍，因为我们做出了结果，他们也看到了，

turns.en: as they start to get the benefits from it, they're like, oh, great, I want to go do more of that. Then we can start raising the bar in terms of our goals and what we want to accomplish together.
turns.zh: 尝到好处之后他们说：太好了，我想做得更多。于是我们就能开始抬高目标、抬高我们一起想达成的标准。

turns.en: We try to be thoughtful about how do you make sure you do that effectively? How do you think about taking a business that's had a certain cadence of growth and inflecting it organically? In mid-sized companies, usually they have grown nicely, but there's something that we can unlock in the business. That's what we want to focus on, is how do we understand what that is? In some business, it may be expanding into new markets.
turns.zh: 我们用心思考怎么做才能确保它真正有效。怎么看待一家已有某种增长节奏的企业，把它有机地推向拐点？在中型公司里，通常增长得不错，但企业内部总有我们可以释放的东西。这就是我们要聚焦的：怎么理解它是什么。有的企业可能是进入新市场。

turns.en: The case of Marine Concepts, one of our companies, it was building out a dealer network in the Southeast. In the case of JMTest, it was driving productivity improvements and focused on customer experience at each of their locations. When we think about earnings growth, 35%. Kager that we've had in our companies, the vast majority of that's organic. We're not doing that through acquisition. We're focused on how do we enhance and improve what they're doing today.
turns.zh: 比如我们的公司 Marine Concepts，它是在东南部建经销商网络。在 JM Test 那边，是提升生产力、专注每个网点的客户体验。我们旗下公司大约 35% 的 CAGR（年均复合增长率）里，绝大部分是内生的，不是靠并购做出来的。我们聚焦的是如何加强和改善他们今天在做的事。

turns.en: Almost all mid-sized companies, there's some opportunity that they haven't been able to focus on. We recently partnered with a business, Keep Supply. It's an amazing industrial refrigeration business. They've compounded that business at 70 plus percent for the last five years.
turns.zh: 几乎每家中型公司都有一些他们无暇顾及的机会。我们最近和一家叫 Keep Supply 的企业结成合伙，非常出色的工业制冷生意，过去五年以超过 70% 的速度复利增长。

turns.en: When they've been growing so fast and taking share, they haven't focused on the customer segmentation or vendor relationships. We can say, here's some opportunities where you have had the time and the resources to help understand what's possible there. We're going to come alongside you and continue to drive growth and improve the business in these fundamental ways.
turns.zh: 他们一直在高速增长、抢占份额，就没那么关注客户分层和供应商关系。我们就可以说：这里有一些机会——以前你们没有时间和资源去看清那里的可能性——我们站到你们身边，继续驱动增长，在这些基本功上改善业务。

turns.en: Each business is so different. It's coming alongside them and understanding that, saying, how can we be helpful? You mentioned at the outset that even though you're going to tend to hold businesses for a long time, some will pay dividends. There could be return to capital recaps. How do you go about making capital allocation decisions at these small, mid-sized companies? We think of capital allocation decisions on multiple levels.
turns.zh: 每家企业都太不一样了。关键是站在他们身边，去理解，去问：我们怎么帮上忙？你一开始提到，尽管你们倾向于长期持有企业，但有些会分红，也可能有资本返还式的再融资 (recap)。你们在这些小型、中型公司里怎么做资本配置决策？我们分多个层面来想。

turns.en: The obvious is acquisitions. There's also the CapEx in terms of, we're going to invest in a new factory or new facility or we're going to expand in some area. Then there's hiring. We think of capital allocation across that spectrum, trying to help them understand, if you invest $100,000 in this role, that means you have $100,000 less that you can go do over here. Does that make sense? Is that trade-off? Getting people to think like owners, act like owners as they're
turns.zh: 显而易见的是并购；还有资本开支 (CapEx)——比如投建新工厂、新设施，或在某个区域扩张。然后是招聘。我们把资本配置放在这个光谱上思考，帮他们理解：如果在这个岗位投 10 万美元，就意味着那边少 10 万美元可花。值不值？这就是取舍。让每个人像所有者一样思考、像所有者一样行动，

turns.en: investing in the full suite of options. As we start getting to acquisitions, we have team members on our side who come alongside them to help think about capital allocation. What is a good investment? What are the criteria that are important?
turns.zh: 在投资所有选项时都带着这个视角。当我们开始进入并购时，我们这边有成员和他们并肩工作，一起思考资本配置：什么是好的投资？什么标准是重要的？

turns.en: Valuation. How do we think about integration? That's important to us. We may not focus on acquisitions right away in a business because there's so much opportunity in the core or there's so much capability we need to build and muscle. We don't want to go do it until we have that. But it's important for us to think about capital allocation in a broad sense. All of these other touchpoints, getting each employee to be thinking about it with that mindset, making the
turns.zh: 估值，以及我们如何看待整合——这对我们很重要。我们对一家企业可能不会马上聚焦并购，因为核心里机会太多，或者我们要建立的肌肉和能力还不足，不准备好就不动。但从广义上思考资本配置很重要。所有这些触点，让每个员工都带着这种心态思考，

turns.en: best decisions that they can for the business. When you're buying a business with a good mode at a reasonable price, implementing your system to help grow it, still a good business, how do you think about exit strategy? Too many firms exit businesses too soon. When you have a great business that's compounding at 20% plus a year, you'd rather continue to hold that and compound it than try to go find a business you know less well that has more risk that you have
turns.zh: 为企业做他们能做的最好决定。当你用一个合理的价格买入一家有很强护城河的企业，落地你们的系统帮它成长，它依然是门好生意时，你们怎么考虑退出战略？太多的企业退出得太早。当你有一个每年以 20% 以上复利增长的伟大企业时，你更愿意继续持有它、让它复利，而不是去找一个你了解更少、风险更多、你还要

turns.en: to go invest in. The traditional fund structure pushes you to exit those businesses prematurely. We want to continue to own those, have that opportunity to compound those, still give opportunity for investors to have liquidity along the way through recaps or other mechanisms. Focus on how do we build? We still look at is a business ready for exit?
turns.zh: 重新去投入学习的企业。传统的基金结构推着你过早退出。我们想继续持有那些企业，享受复利的机会，同时通过再融资 (recap) 等机制让投资人在中途获得流动性。我们聚焦于怎么建设。我们依然会看这家企业是否到了该退出的时候：

turns.en: What's the market going to pay this? What do we think the future growth of the business might look like? What do we think the risks are to the company? Usually the risk is exiting too soon versus exiting too late. We'd rather continue to compound, especially if we can turn capital along the way for investors. At what point in time would you look to sell?
turns.zh: 市场会付什么价？我们怎么看企业未来的增长？我们怎么看公司面临的风险？通常风险是退出太早，而不是太晚。我们更愿意继续复利，尤其当我们还能中途为投资者返还资本时。什么时点你们会选择卖？

turns.en: There's a few things. Let's say the market is going to pay us a silly price that it's going to be hard for us to achieve ourselves. That might be a candidate or the market looks risky in the future.
turns.zh: 有几种情况。假设市场愿意给我们一个我们自己很难实现的荒谬高价，那可能是个候选；或者未来市场看起来风险很大。

turns.en: We've driven a lot of growth in the business. There's something changing. It's a business that's going to be affected by AI that comes along and we think that the future earnings are more risky than they are today. That might be a candidate. Maybe there's a future home for the business that is a better home for us. It's a partner that can help accelerate in a way that we can't today.
turns.zh: 或者我们已经驱动了企业大量增长，但有些东西在变。比如一个会被 AI 冲击的业务冒出来，我们认为未来的盈利比今天更不确定，那可能是个候选。又或者，也许有一个比我们更适合的归宿——一个能比我们更好地加速它的伙伴。

turns.en: They'll pay us for the earnings of the business that we've had. We think it's a better home for the business. Those are all factors. When you step back from owning one business to a portfolio of companies, how have you thought about the breadth of different types of businesses you want to own? When I was at Berkshire, we had a number of businesses, 60 plus core holdings, plus a number of subsidiaries in all different industries. I grew up in an environment where
turns.zh: 他们愿意为我们已经做出的盈利付钱，我们也认为那是企业更好的归宿。这些都是考量。当你从拥有单一企业退后一步，看整个组合时，你们怎么思考要持有的业务类型的广度？我在 Berkshire 时，我们有 60 多个核心持仓，加上大量子公司，遍布所有行业。我是在一个

turns.en: it wasn't specialized. It was a generalist approach. At Canberra, we're more specialized than that, but we're not going to be deep sector specialists. We're going to focus on the highest quality businesses that we can grow and compound. We think the business system works regardless of industry or space at this size and stage. We can help grow it, the overarching portfolio and approach is bringing more high quality businesses that are compounding, creating a system that
turns.zh: 非专业化、通才式的环境里成长的。Canvas 比那更聚焦，但我们也不会做深度的行业专家。我们要聚焦于能找到的最高质量的企业，去增长、去复利。我们相信这套业务系统在这个规模和阶段下适用于任何行业和领域，我们能帮它成长。整个组合和方式的大逻辑，是纳入更多高质量、能复利的企业，搭建一个

turns.en: allows us to help the businesses build the muscle in the companies. What we find over time is they own more and more of what they're driving and what they're doing. We're coming alongside them building the muscle. By having a longer term duration, we have benefit of doing that. If we're going to exit a business in four years, it doesn't make sense to build the muscle deep in the business, or if we're going to own a business for 10 plus years, there's a benefit of doing that. That's
turns.zh: 帮助企业在公司内部建立肌肉的系统。我们发现，随着时间推移，他们对自己驱动的事情掌控得越来越多，而我们站在身边帮他们建立能力。正因为我们的持有期长，这样做才有好处。如果我们 4 年后就要卖掉一家企业，就没有必要在组织深处建立肌肉；但如果我们要持有 10 年以上，那样做是有价值的。

turns.en: how we think about the construction. If we think about the management, how do we create a system to manage it that allows us to buy the highest quality businesses, grow and compound them over time, treat them like we'd want to be treated if they were our businesses.
turns.zh: 这就是我们对组合搭建的思考：怎么创建一个管理系统，让我们能买入最高质量的企业、长期持有并复利增长，并且像希望别人对待我们自己的企业那样对待它们。

turns.en: Should have owned seven. What's the difference between the marginal company that you have partnered with and one that you were very close to but didn't?
turns.zh: 本来该是七家。你最终合伙的最边缘的那家企业，和那些非常接近却没成的，差别是什么？

turns.en: We look at about 500 investments to do one or two. When we look at a business that's right on the cost, there's usually a couple of things that happen. There might be a business that we'd invest in, but they decide to continue to own it. That usually is the most likely path. If it's something we like, it's not that they're selling to someone else. They usually just decide, I'm not going to sell right now. That's great for us. We'd love to stay in touch if that's the case. The businesses
turns.zh: 我们大约看 500 个机会才做一两笔。当一家企业处在临界线上时，通常有几种情况。有一种是我们愿意投，但所有者决定继续自己持有。这往往是最可能的走向。如果是我们喜欢的企业，通常也不是他们卖给了别人，而是他们决定现在不卖。这对我们反而好，这种情况下我们很乐意保持联系。至于那些

turns.en: that are on the cost of us passing on, either we can't get comfortable with the industry, some dynamics, growth, challenges, the moats there, but it's not as strong as we'd like, or there's some aspect that it might get disrupted over time. Sometimes we're just not aligned with management in terms of their vision of the future, or we're concerned about how they'll show up or how they'll engage with us. Those would be other ones that are on the cost. We want to
turns.zh: 处在临界线上、我们放弃的企业：要么我们对行业、某些动态、增长、挑战或护城河不够安心——护城河没那么强；要么它可能被某种东西颠覆；有时候是我们和管理层在对未来的愿景上不一致，或者我们担心他们会如何行事、如何与我们共事。这些也是放弃的理由。我们要保持高标准，

turns.en: continue to have a high bar in terms of the quality of businesses we have, being selective and making sure the ones that we partner with are aligned with us in terms of vision and values that we think will compound nicely over time. I'd love you to take me through one of your portfolio companies, soup to nuts, and for fun, maybe pick the one that's been most challenged relative to your expectations. One of our earliest is an aftermarket marine business. They sell high-end
turns.zh: 保持对高质量企业的严格筛选，确保我们合伙的企业在愿景和价值观上与我们一致，并且我们认为它们能漂亮地长期复利。我想请你带我从头到尾走一遍你的一家企业——好玩的是，挑那家与你预期落差最大的。我们最早的投资之一是一家售后市场的船舶业务，卖高端

turns.en: boat covers. It was started by Randy Kent, who was a boating enthusiast, loved boating, but hated covering his boat at the end. It's a 30-minute process. He invented this track system that sits above the boat. The cover drops around the boat, and then you zip it up. It takes two minutes to cover your boat. He invented the system, patented it. They have IP on the track system.
turns.zh: 船罩。创始人是 Randy Kent，他是个船迷，酷爱开船，但讨厌最后给船盖罩子的过程——要 30 分钟。他发明了一套轨道系统，装在船上方，罩子沿轨道落下来包住船，再拉上拉链，两分钟就能盖好。他发明了这套系统并申请了专利，他们在轨道系统上有知识产权。

turns.en: Solved a pain point that bone owners had. Launched in Lake of the Ozarks. Business had NPS in the 60s. Great NPS. Customers loved it. He had grown it and wasn't interested in taking it to the next level. He was more interested in other pursuits. He connected with us because he was interested in a partner and scaling and growing it. We saw this opportunity to build out a dealer network.
turns.zh: 它解决了船主的痛点。产品在 Lake of the Ozarks 起家，企业的 NPS 在 60 多——非常好的分数，客户很喜欢。他把它发展起来，但没兴趣把它带到下一个层级，他更关心其他追求。他找到我们，因为他想找合伙人来扩张和增长。我们看到建经销商网络的机会，

turns.en: That was exciting to us, helping take the company to the next level. We partnered with them. It was smaller than we usually look at. A couple million in EBITDA. We usually look above five million and above. In hindsight, what we learned from that is that's a hard stage for us. The business system gets more value as there's more earnings in the company. We prefer businesses that are five million in earnings up versus two. Our first mistake there was just
turns.zh: 这让我们很兴奋——帮企业进入下一个阶段。我们和它结成合伙。它比我们的常规标的要小，EBITDA 只有几百万美元，我们通常看 500 万以上。事后看，我们从中学到：那个阶段对我们很难。企业利润越厚，业务系统能创造的价值越大。我们更愿意持有利润 500 万以上而非 200 万的企业。在那里的第一个失误，

turns.en: it was a smaller stage than we were accustomed to. Our second mistake is we brought in the wrong leader. The owner wanted to transition out. It was part of the process. We hired a leader who had strong industry experience. He had grown and scaled a similar type of marine business.
turns.zh: 就是规模比我们的舒适区小。第二个失误是我们找错了领导者。业主想退出，这是过程的一部分。我们雇了一位行业经验丰富的领导者，他做成并扩大过一个类似的船舶业务。

turns.en: We over-indexed on that strength of that experience. Building a dealer network was harder for him and harder for the team than they had expected. We were trying to help him and it culturally wasn't a great fit. The learning there was not only do you need someone with experience, but you need a strong culture fit and alignment. Fortunately, we hired Steve Handel, who joined us 18 months ago.
turns.zh: 我们过于看重那一条经验的优势了。建经销商网络对他、对团队都比预期更难。我们努力帮他，但在文化上并不契合。那里的教训是：不仅需要有经验的人，还需要很强的文化契合和对齐。幸运的是，我们雇了 Steve Handel，他 18 个月前加入我们，

turns.en: He'd been at Red Ventures and then in an operating business. He's done an amazing job. He's course corrected in terms of the dealer network build out. The business is in a much better place now. We've doubled the size of it. A lot of growth and opportunity there.
turns.zh: 之前在 Red Ventures，也在运营企业干过。他做得非常棒，把经销商网络的扩张纠正回了正轨。企业现在好多了，我们已经把它做大了两倍，有很多成长和机会。

turns.en: The starting point was a tough one and then some mistakes that Brian and I made along the way. High quality business still has the strength and the moat, still has the opportunity. We much rather be spending our time at five million EBITDA businesses than two.
turns.zh: 起点很艰难，然后是 Brian 和我一路犯的一些错。高质量的生意依然有优势、有护城河、有机会。我们更愿意把时间花在 EBITDA 500 万的企业上，而不是 200 万的。

turns.en: How about one that's right in your speed spot? JMTest is a great example. We partnered with the Morrison family, 40-year-old family business.
turns.zh: 那来一家正好在你们甜蜜区 (sweet spot) 的？JM Test 是个很好的例子。我们和 Morrison 家族合伙，一家 40 年的家族企业。

turns.en: They had grown nicely over time. They wanted an alternative to traditional PE. They had talked to a number of private equity firms connected with us. They're in the calibration services space.
turns.zh: 他们这些年增长得不错，想要传统私募股权之外的另一种选择。他们和很多私募股权公司聊过，然后和我们接上了。他们做计量校准服务。

turns.en: They calibrate industrial equipment. Anything that measures flow, pressure, temperature, electricity, great business. Sticky customers don't change. It's a small purchase price relative to the cost of failure of the products. That business has forex since we partnered with it three plus years ago. There's opportunity to continue to grow and partner with other regional players.
turns.zh: 他们给工业设备做校准——凡是测流量、压力、温度、电力的东西。好生意：客户粘性高，不会换。它的采购金额小，对应的是产品失效的巨大成本。这家企业自我们合伙的三年多以来一直在产生自由现金流 (free cash flow)。有机会继续增长，和其他区域性玩家合作。

turns.en: The owner wanted to transition out over a couple of years. We brought in Andrew Tenor, who is someone we worked with previously. He's been a strong leader in helping accelerate that.
turns.zh: 业主想在几年内退出，我们带来了之前合作过的 Andrew Tenor，他是一位强有力的领导者，帮助加速了这一切。

turns.en: We've had a lot of great talent in that business. We've been able to support the leadership there. A lot of opportunity. Very exciting to see the growth and the progress of that.
turns.zh: 这家企业里有很多优秀的人才，我们一直支持那里的领导层，机会很多。看到它的成长和进步非常令人兴奋。

turns.en: Also, a business that we think continues to compound and is a nice growth story. What is the team around Brian and you executing the strategy?
turns.zh: 也是我们觉得会继续复利、增长故事很美的生意。Brian 和你身边执行战略的团队是什么样的？

turns.en: We have a team of 16 three key areas. Our investing team, which is focused on the companies we're investing in, the diligence, the research, keeping that high quality bar.
turns.zh: 我们的团队共 16 人，分三个关键领域。投资团队，专注于我们投资的企业——尽调、研究、守住高质量标准。

turns.en: Our community team, which is building the relationships with owners and partners well ahead of partnership or transaction. Then our Cambridge Business System team, that's our largest team. It'll always be our largest team. That's the team that's coming alongside the owners and working with them. They are a combination of generalists, also specialists focusing on topics like talent or finance, tech and AI, recruiting, those types of topics, the hands-on partner that
turns.zh: 社群团队，在合伙或交易之前很久就与业主和伙伴建立关系。然后是 Canvas 业务系统团队，我们最大的团队，也会永远是最大的团队。他们是站到业主身边、和他们一起工作的人，既有通才也有专才，分别专注人才、财务、技术和 AI、招聘等话题，是陪伴企业整个生命周期的实干伙伴。

turns.en: continues with the company throughout life. Where are you hoping to take the business from here? We want to be the best business builders in the world. We want to help organizations and people reach their full potential. That's what we're focused on. There's a lot of opportunity to go do that.
turns.zh: 陪伴企业走完全程。你们希望把 Canvas 带到哪里？我们想成为世界上最好的企业建设者。我们想帮助组织和个人发挥全部潜能。这是我们聚焦的方向，那里有巨大的机会。

turns.en: There's this growing group of families and founders who want something different, unique and special. Our hope is to continue to build that for decades to come. Brian and I are still young in our careers. That gives us a long runway. In addition to our companies compounding and having that long runway, we think there's this great opportunity to compound what we're building at Canberra with a long runway and investing in a great team to go do that.
turns.zh: 有越来越多的家族和创始人想要不一样的、独特而特别的东西。我们希望未来几十年持续建设它。我和 Brian 在职业生涯里还很年轻，这给了我们很长的跑道。在我们的企业复利增长、跑道很长的同时，我们相信让 Canvas 所打造的事业复利、投入一支优秀的团队去做这件事，同样是巨大的机会。

turns.en: Trace, I want to make sure I get a chance to ask you a couple of fun closing questions. What was your first paid job and what did you learn from it?
turns.zh: Tracy，我想确保有机会问你几个轻松的收尾问题。你的第一份有薪工作是什么？你从中学到了什么？

turns.en: I started on our family's farm working. I was in first grade making 50 cents an hour working on the farm, running the cash register. I couldn't even reach the cash register. I had to stand on a turnover milk crate to reach it. It taught me so much work ethic, integrity, business from that vantage point. I'm fortunate to have had that experience.
turns.zh: 我最早在自家农场干活，一年级时每小时 50 美分，在农场管收银机。我连收银机都够不着，得站在一个倒扣的牛奶板条箱上才够得着。那教会了我太多：勤劳、正直，还有从那个视角看生意。我很幸运有过那段经历。

turns.en: What have you changed your mind about the last few years? AI is affecting everybody and people are thinking a lot about it. When I first came out, I thought a lot about what it would change, what it would do to all of us in the white color world, especially how do we think about intelligence, working and what that looks like. It'll still be disruptive, but I believe now that the people, the culture, the relationships will be even more
turns.zh: 过去几年你改变了什么想法？AI 在影响每一个人，大家都在思考它。我刚接触它时，想的多是它会改变什么、对我们这些白领世界意味着什么——尤其是怎么思考智能、工作以及它们的形态。它依然会是颠覆性的，但我现在相信：人、文化、关系会变得更加重要。

turns.en: important. I thought for a while, will you need that as much? That's even more important now than another has been. We're under invested in that as a society and there'll be this great opportunity to invest in that more. Which two people have had the biggest impact on your professional life? Hands down, Warren Buffett had a tremendous impact on me, both in terms of giving me an opportunity when I had little experience, the trust and confidence that he had in me over time,
turns.zh: 我曾有一段时间觉得还需要这些吗？现在它们比以往任何时候都更重要。整个社会在这一点上投入不足，未来会有巨大的机会去更多地投入。哪两个人对你的职业生涯影响最大？毫无疑问，Warren Buffett。他对我影响巨大——在我几乎没什么经验时就给我机会，随着时间推移给我的信任和信心，

turns.en: the types of opportunities that he gave me. The other I'd say is my husband, he's affected my personal life and our family life even more so my professional career.
turns.zh: 还有他给我的那些机会。另一个我会说是我的先生——他对我个人生活和家庭生活的影响甚至比对职业生涯更大。

turns.en: It is especially important that the person you marry is supportive of what you're doing, especially for women. It's the most important career decision. Do you have a supportive partner who can be there as a sounding board, can help you, also flexible and willing to believe in you?
turns.zh: 你嫁的那个人支持你做的事尤其重要，对女性尤其如此。这是最重要的职业决定。你有没有一个支持型的伴侣，能做你的商量对象，能帮你，并且灵活、愿意相信你？

turns.en: My husband, Scott, has been that and more. I couldn't have done what I've done without him and his support. Those would be the two. What's a life lesson you wish you learned earlier in life?
turns.zh: 我的先生 Scott 做到的远不止这些。没有他的支持，我不可能做成我做的一切。就是这两个人。有什么人生道理是你希望早点学到的？

turns.en: One would be when you trust and believe in people, you help them. You can get more so out of anybody than if you are too involved, too overriding, too micromanaging. Warren believed in me and I saw that trust. I've seen it even more so in the work that I've done. I wish I would have learned that even sooner. Tracy, last one. If the next five years are a chapter in your life, what's that chapter about? It's about building. At Canberra, we're building something special and unique for
turns.zh: 一个就是：当你信任并相信一个人、去帮助他们，你能从任何人身上激发出远比过度介入、过度指挥、过度微观管理更多的东西。Warren 相信过我，我看到了那份信任，在我后来的工作里体会更深。我希望我更早学到这一点。Tracy，最后一个：如果未来五年是你人生的一章，这一章讲的是什么？

turns.en: this next generation of companies. This first chapter has been building the foundation. Now we have a strong foundation. It's what we can build from here.
